newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Standard Chartered M.L. put on rating watch.
newsitem.headline: Standard Chartered M.L. put on rating watch.

text.p: The Pakistan Credit Rating Agency (PACRA) said on Friday it had placed Standard Chartered Mercantile Leasing Co Ltd (SCML) on rating watch.
A PACRA statement said its action followed the reported sale of Standard Chartered Bank's shareholding in SCML to Saudi Pak Industrial and Agricultural Investment Co (Pvt) Ltd (SAPICO).

PACRA said it had assigned a long-term rating of A-plus and a short-term rating of A1 to SCML in December 1995 and confirmed these ratings in January 1997, partly because Standard Chartered Bank's financial support was implied in any contingency.
"With the termination of Standard Chartered's equity stake, the bank's implied support would no longer be available.

"While PACRA recognises the large asset size and financial strength of the new institutional investor (SAPICO), it would like to reassess the support factor as well as the capacity of SAPICO to provide such support before deciding on the new rating," the statement from the Lahore-based agency said.

SCML's 10-rupee stock fell 0.90 rupees, or 4.31 percent, to 20, at the Karachi Stock Exchange on Friday, the day after the Standard Chartered Group in Pakistan announced plans to sell its stake in the company to SAPICO for an undisclosed price.
SAPICO is a joint venture between the governments of Saudi Arabia and Pakistan and its chairman is nominated by Riyadh.

PACRA, Pakistan's first credit rating agency, was set up in 1994 as a joint venture by the British-based credit rating agency IBCA, the International Finance Corporation and the Lahore Stock Exchange.
